title: certainlyscraped run contract
description: Output contract for `certainlyscraped run` (also `cscrape run`). A run is only a success when it extracts at least min_rows records (counted before any --since filtering) and no page ended incomplete. Exit codes are part of the contract. The run report is JSONL, one PageOutcome per line; the MCP `scrape` tool returns the same records in its `pages` array plus a status word.
command: certainlyscraped run <config.yaml> [--out <dataset>|-] [--min-rows N] [--sample N] [--since PREV] [--key FIELD]... [--snapshot PATH] [--report PATH] [--accept-partial] [--proxies PATH | --no-proxy]

exit_codes.0: complete: at least min-rows records and no incomplete page (--accept-partial maps 4 to 0)
exit_codes.1: config, I/O or fetch error; with --min-rows 0, a run whose every page errored
exit_codes.2: fewer than min-rows records scraped (an empty result fails loudly); 2 wins over 4. An all-error run at the default --min-rows 1 has no records, so it is 2, not 1
exit_codes.4: incomplete: at least min-rows records, but one or more pages ended blocked, rate_limited or error after all retries

mcp_statuses.complete: at least min_rows rows and no incomplete page
mcp_statuses.incomplete: at least min_rows rows, but one or more pages ended blocked, rate_limited or error
mcp_statuses.blocked: zero rows and every page was blocked or rate_limited
mcp_statuses.error: zero rows and every page errored

page_outcomes.ok: the page was fetched and classified as real content; rows may be any count
page_outcomes.empty: the page was fetched and classified ok, but extracted zero rows
page_outcomes.blocked: a challenge page, a plain 403, or no proxy was available for the host
page_outcomes.error: no response, a 5xx, or another status that is not a wall

artifacts.path: --out value (default out.csv); - writes the dataset to stdout
artifacts.rows: every scraped row, or with --since only new/changed rows plus a `_change` column

artifacts.format: inferred from the extension, else the config `output:` key

artifacts.rows: one JSON object per attempted page, in page order, whatever the run's exit code

stderr: [probe] <url> -> tier <t> (<note>)   (tier: auto only; skipped when a proxy pool is configured)
[done] <pages> pages: <n> ok, <n> empty, <n> not_found, <n> blocked, <n> rate_limited, <n> error (HTTP <status> on <path>)
[done] ... (no response on <path>)   (the first incomplete page had status 0)
[since] <path> not found: every row is new
[run] incomplete: <n> page(s) blocked/rate-limited/errored; rows may be missing (exit 4; --accept-partial to accept)

page_outcome.description: One attempted page. Written to --report (JSONL) and returned by the MCP `scrape` tool in `pages`.

url.description: the page URL that was fetched

status.description: HTTP status, 0 when no response arrived

rows.description: rows extracted from this page after dedupe

attempts.description: fetch attempts spent on this page (1 + retries/climbs used); 0 when no proxy was available for the host, so no fetch ran

steps.description: each rung tried, in order, with the leased proxy group when a pool is configured, e.g. ["t1@dc-a", "t1@dc-b", "t2@dc-b"]. With a pool every step has @group; with no pool none does

proxy_group.description: group label of the leased proxy, or null when fetching directly; never a proxy address

note.description: why the page ended this way, e.g. 'challenge page: cloudflare' or 'max_tier 2 reached'. A page with status 0 keeps the last transport error text instead (scrubbed), e.g. 'ConnectionError: ... over proxy ***' or 'DNSError: ... Could not resolve host ...'

mcp_scrape.description: The MCP `scrape` tool's result object. Every tool result is a JSON object on the wire, including refusals; a tool never raises.

dataset_path.description: full JSONL dataset under <workdir>/.certainlyscraped/; null when the request was refused before a run (bad config, a guard refusal during the tier: auto probe, an exception), not when individual pages errored: those still produce a dataset (an explicit tier refuses at fetch time and the page outcome carries the error)

notes.description: clamps, truncation and refusals, in the order they applied

private_refused.description: present and true only when the guard refused the target during the initial tier probe (config tier: auto); an explicit tier still refuses the fetch but does not set this field
